## Claims
- [source-backed] \(\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\) has Schur \(\mathbb Z\)-basis \(\{s_\lambda\}\), and the span \(I_{r,n-r}\) of \(s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\) is an ideal; hence \(A:=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\). [source-2, lines 1310-1324]
- [source-backed] For \(\rho=i^j\) and \(B=(n-r)^r\), the relevant Bruhat condition is Young-diagram containment, and \(J_v\) is generated by \(\{s_\mu:\rho\subseteq\mu\subseteq B\}\). [source-2, lines 1365-1375]
- [proved] Put \(\mathcal U=\{\mu:\rho\subseteq\mu\subseteq B\}\), \(F=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathcal U}\mathbb Z e_\mu\), and identify \(F\cong J_v\) by \(e_\mu\mapsto s_\mu\). For partitions \(\varnothing\ne\lambda\subseteq B\), \(\mu\in\mathcal U\), write in \(\Lambda\)
  \[
  s_\lambda s_\mu=\sum_\nu c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}s_\nu,
  \]
  and set
  \[
  r_{\lambda,\mu}:=\sum_{\nu\in\mathcal U}c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}e_\nu.
  \]
  Then there is an exact integral presentation
  \[
  Q:=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong
  \frac{\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathcal U}\mathbb Z e_\mu}
       {\left\langle r_{\lambda,\mu}:
       \varnothing\ne\lambda\subseteq B,\ \mu\in\mathcal U\right\rangle_{\mathbb Z}}.
  \]
  Indeed, terms \(s_\nu\) with \(\nu\not\subseteq B\) vanish in \(A\), by the definition of \(I_{r,n-r}\); this is the box truncation. Since \(s_\lambda s_\mu\in J_v\) and the displayed Schur classes form the basis of \(J_v\), the surviving terms have \(\nu\in\mathcal U\). Thus the relation subgroup maps onto \(\Lambda_+J_v\). Conversely, every positive-degree element of \(A\) is a \(\mathbb Z\)-linear combination of \(s_\lambda\) with \(\varnothing\ne\lambda\subseteq B\), while every element of \(J_v\) is a \(\mathbb Z\)-linear combination of \(s_\mu\), \(\mu\in\mathcal U\). Bilinearity therefore expresses every element of \(\Lambda_+J_v\) as a \(\mathbb Z\)-linear combination of the listed products. Hence the relation subgroup is precisely \(\Lambda_+J_v\).
- [source-backed] The two proposed smaller Schur generating families are
  \[
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},
  \qquad
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\},
  \]
  where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\); each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-6, lines 14-42]
- [conjectural] Smith normal form of the displayed presentation matrix is expected to give \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), and hence establish irredundance of both smaller Schur families; the supplied record states that this stronger statement was not proved in the source. [source-6, lines 56-72]

## Strategy
Use the finite matrix whose rows are the coefficient vectors \(r_{\lambda,\mu}\). Its Smith normal form gives the rank, torsion, and minimum integral generator number of \(Q\).

## Gaps
- No Smith-normal-form computation or uniform rank argument is supplied.
- Therefore this presentation does not prove \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) or minimality of the two smaller families.

## Next
Compute the Smith normal form symbolically or prove matching lower bounds for \(Q/pQ\) for every prime \(p\).
